newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DALGLISH ERA BEGINS AGAINST TRICKY CUP OPPONENTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DALGLISH ERA BEGINS AGAINST TRICKY CUP OPPONENTS.

text.p: Kenny Dalglish will not be in charge of Newcastle when they play first division Charlton Athletic in an F.A. Cup third round replay at St James' Park on Wednesday -- but Dalglish has good reason to fear the damage they can inflict on his new side.
Dalglish, named as Newcastle's new manager on Tuesday, was boss of a high-flying Blackburn team who were humbled by Charlton in a Cup replay three years ago.
Blackburn went into the tie unbeaten in 10 Cup and league matches, but after securing a 0-0 fourth round draw at Charlton, they lost 1-0 at home in the replay. It was a major upset.

Both David Batty and Alan Shearer, who should play against Charlton on Wednesday, were in that Blackburn side -- and Charlton and Manchester United were the only teams Shearer failed to score against during a 14-match spell that spanned those two Cup games and brought him a haul of 15 goals.

Oddly, Newcastle have never beaten Charlton in the Cup, losing in the semifinal in 1947 and in the third round the following year . Those were their only previous meetings until their 1-1 draw at Charlton on January 5.

Another curious aspect is that the Dalglish era begins at Newcastle in the middle of a Cup tie -- in the same way that his reign at Liverpool ended. On February 20, 1991, Liverpool and Everton drew 4-4 at Goodison Park in one of the most exciting Cup matches in living memory.

The original game had ended goalless at Anfield three days before and as the clubs were preparing for a second replay back at Goodison the following week, Dalglish quit Liverpool, sparking the same kind of anguish and astonishment which followed Kevin Keegan's departure from Newcastle last week. Everton subsequently won the second replay 1-0.

Dalglish will watch Wednesday's match with his former Liverpool team mate, assistant manager Terry McDermott, and chief scout Arthur Cox in charge of the team. They were also running the show when Newcastle drew 2-2 with Aston Villa on Saturday.
Dalglish said at Tuesday's news conference held to announce his arrival that he had no immediate plans to change any of his backroom staff.
Confirming that McDermott and Cox were very much part of his plans, Dalglish said: "Terry and Arthur have prepared the team for tomorrow night and it wouldn't be fair of me to take over.

"Terry Mac will stay here. He's someone I know I can trust and the same goes for Arthur. He has got a vast knowledge of Newcastle football club and it would be wrong of me to dismiss that. I can learn from it."
McDermott played together with Dalglish for Liverpool as did Peter Beardsley, who, even though he turns 36 this month, is still an integral part of Newcastle's plans.

With Mark Lawrenson brought to Newcastle by Keegan to coach the defence, Dalglish links up with many old friends at St James' Park. He will also come across a familiar face on Saturday in his first official match in charge.
Newcastle travel to Southampton in the premier league where his former Liverpool team mate Graeme Souness will be there to greet him.
